html:
The Kadambas were a royal family of north Karnataka and the Konkan coast, ruling from Banavasi from about 345 to the mid 6th century.

Legend says the founder, Mayurasharma, was a Brahmin student insulted by a guard at the Pallava capital of Kanchi. He gave up his studies, took up the sword and carved out a kingdom in the forests. The Kadambas were the first native rulers to use Kannada in government; the Halmidi inscription of the 5th century is the oldest known Kannada inscription.

They married into the Western Gangas and even the Guptas. In the 6th century the Chalukyas of Badami, once their vassals, overpowered them, and later Kadamba branches survived only as local chiefs, as in Goa.
sum: The Kadambas were a royal family of north Karnataka and the Konkan coast, ruling from Banavasi from about 345 to the mid 6th century.
